1. Start with the inspection records.

completion:
If a sample result is higher than the Maximum Contaminant Level (MCL), send the sample for re-analysis.
3. If the second sample result is still higher than the MCL, immediately take the following actions:
   a. Send the second sample result to the laboratory requesting re-analysis.
   b. Immediately apply corrective action (e.g. shut off water service, notify customers, switch to alternative water supply, etc.)
   c. Notify the Connecticut Department of Public Health (DPH) within 24 hours of receipt of the second sample result.
   d. Immediately provide for alternative safe drinking water.
   e. Begin process of data verification.
   f. Initiate any necessary treatment to return the water to be within the MCL.
   g. If failure is "confirmed" (see below) by additional analysis, continue monitoring until contamination is below the MCL for at least three consecutive
